old: Connectors of Result: ezért and így
new: Recap: ezért and mert
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (mert-because, a1-119-b)

old: To express logical results and consequences, Hungarian uses *ezért* ('therefore / that is why') and *így* ('thus / in this way'). Notice that *ezért* connects an observed environmental fact with an action or outcome: *Sok műanyaghulladék keletkezik, ezért szelektíven gyűjtjük a szemetet.*
new: You know *mert* ('because') and *ezért* ('so, that is why') from A1 Unit 24: *mert* gives the reason, *ezért* gives the result; *így* ('this way, so') also leads into a result. Here you use them for the environment: *Sok a műanyaghulladék, ezért fontos a szelektív hulladékgyűjtés.*
why: the screen presents a form an earlier unit taught as new; rewritten as a recap (mert-because, a1-119-b)

why: the screen presents kell + inflected infinitive (A1 Unit 24, A2 Unit 41) as new and mentions hogy + subjunctive (B1 Unit 5); recap

old: When discussing ecological duties, *kell* combines with inflected infinitives (*meg kell tennünk* - 'we must do') or subjunctive clauses (*szükséges, hogy óvjuk* - 'it is necessary that we protect').
new: You know *kell* + infinitive from A1 Unit 24 and the infinitive with personal endings from A2 Unit 41: the ending shows who has to act (*tennem kell*, *tenned kell*, *tennie kell*, *tennünk kell*). Here you use them for what people have to do for the environment: *Sokat kell tennünk a környezetvédelemért.*
why: the screen presents kell + inflected infinitive (A1 Unit 24, A2 Unit 41) as new and mentions hogy + subjunctive (B1 Unit 5); recap

old: In formal and expository Hungarian, *emiatt* ('on account of this / due to this') and *aminek következtében* ('as a consequence of which') link broader climatic causes to specific ecological impacts.
new: You know *miatt* ('because of') from A2 Unit 40 (*miattam*, *miatta*). Now two connectors link a whole clause to its result: *emiatt* ('because of this') and the more formal *aminek következtében* ('as a result of which'). *Kevés az eső, és emiatt kevés a víz a tóban.*
why: screen text was a bare gloss list and never said that miatt is known; text names the known part and the new part

old: Environmental Compound Nouns in Hungarian
new: Compound and Possessive Nouns
why: the screen called ökológiai lábnyom (adjective + noun) a compound noun and said nothing about the possessive half of the skill (noun-compounds = possessive and compound nouns)

old: Hungarian forms precise scientific compound nouns: *szén-dioxid-kibocsátás* (written with hyphens due to length/rules), *ökológiai lábnyom*, *klímaváltozás*.
new: Hungarian joins nouns into one word: *klíma + változás = klímaváltozás*, *üveg + ház + hatás = üvegházhatás*, *repülő + út = repülőút*. A long compound of three or more parts is written with hyphens: *szén-dioxid-kibocsátás*. An adjective stays a separate word: *ökológiai lábnyom*. With the possessive ending *-a/-e* (A1 Unit 9) a compound can say whose it is: *az energiaforrások használata* = the use of the energy sources.
why: the screen called ökológiai lábnyom (adjective + noun) a compound noun and said nothing about the possessive half of the skill (noun-compounds = possessive and compound nouns)

old: Real and Unreal Conditions: Ha nem lépünk időben...
new: Recap: ha Clauses
why: the screen presented ha clauses as new and used the past conditional with volna (B1 Unit 39, taught later) and unmet erodálódni

old: Predicting consequences uses real conditions with present or future indicative: *Ha nem védjük az erdőket, a talaj erodálódni fog.* Past or unreal conditions use the conditional: *Ha korábban elkezdtük volna, most jobb helyzetben lennénk.*
new: You know *ha* ('if') from A2 Unit 13 and *ha* + conditional from A2 Unit 28: the *ha* clause names the condition, the other clause says what follows. Here you use it for what happens to nature: *Ha nem vigyázunk a vízre, kevés víz marad.* With the conditional the condition is only imagined: *Ha több fa lenne, tisztább lenne a város.*
why: the screen presented ha clauses as new and used the past conditional with volna (B1 Unit 39, taught later) and unmet erodálódni

old: Rather than passive voice, Hungarian uses reflexive/mediopassive verbs to describe spontaneous or environmental changes: *a folyó szennyeződik* ('the river becomes polluted'), *a természet megújul* ('nature renews itself').
new: You know from A2 Unit 31 that Hungarian often uses a verb that 'happens by itself' (*elromlik*, *megoldódik*) where English would use a passive. Many changes in nature are described this way: *a folyó szennyeződik* ('the river becomes polluted'), *a természet megújul* ('nature renews itself'), *eltűnik az erdő* ('the forest disappears').

new: You know *azért, hogy* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 5: it says why something is done, and the verb after *hogy* ends in *-jon/-jen* (*csökkenjen*, *legyen*). Here you use it for green programmes: *Azért támogatják a zöld átállást, hogy tisztább legyen a levegő.*

why: the rule named energiatakarékosság (from takarékos + -ság, not a verb + -ás/-és) as a verbal noun, and gave no rule for -ás vs -és

old: Verbal nouns ending in *-ás / -és* form the core vocabulary of sustainability: *újrahasznosít* -> *újrahasznosítás*, *takarékoskodik* -> *energiatakarékosság*.
new: A verb becomes a noun for the action with *-ás* after back vowels or *-és* after front vowels: *tanul → tanulás* (studying), *olvas → olvasás* (reading), *pihen → pihenés* (resting), *újrahasznosít → újrahasznosítás* (recycling). A verb in *-ik* drops it: *étkezik → étkezés*. The noun takes the usual endings: *az újrahasznosítást* (accusative), *az újrahasznosításért* (for recycling).
